intro: Denver owns the NFL record for consecutive one-score wins at 16, Houston beat Indianapolis 26-3 on Thursday night, and Tampa Bay waits on Baker Mayfield's foot before Sunday in Detroit. Cincinnati carries a five-game win streak into Washington on Monday night. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Broncos stretch their one-score win streak to an NFL record 16
top.dek: Denver beat Carolina 26-21 on Nov. 8 after Nik Bonitto stripped Bryce Young late and Bo Nix finished the drive with a one-yard sneak. The 16th straight one-score win passed the Colts' mark of 15. The Broncos used their bye to rest and host Las Vegas on Sunday.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Mayfield and Winfield miss practice before Tampa Bay's trip to Detroit
top.dek: Baker Mayfield sat out Wednesday with a foot and right thumb issue, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. missed with an ankle injury. Yaya Diaby was limited with a knee problem. Tristan Wirfs and Cade Otton practiced in full.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Will Anderson Jr. gets first career safety and leads the NFL in sacks
top.dek: Anderson dropped Daniel Jones in the end zone for a safety in Houston's 26-3 win. He finished with seven pressures and four quarterback hits. His 11.5 sacks are the most in the league.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 31%: Green Bay's pass block win rate, worst since 2017
top.dek: TSN, citing ESPN's tracking, says the Packers are on pace for the lowest pass block win rate since the metric began. Green Bay has started four different left guards this season. Jordan Love took eight sacks in the last loss.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Bengals visit the Commanders on Monday night
top.dek: Cincinnati (7-2) plays Washington (3-5-1) at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Bengals rank first in passing offense at 298.8 yards per game. Washington ranks 31st against the pass.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Cook chases an NFL record streak

stories.text: James Cook ties an NFL record with eight straight 75-yard, one-touchdown games
stories.summary: Cook ran for 157 yards and a 74-yard touchdown in Sunday's win at the Jets. That made eight straight games with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing score, matching John Riggins in 1983 and LaDainian Tomlinson in 2006. The 74-yarder was the longest run of his career. A ninth game against Miami would set the record outright.

stories.text: Kincaid, two corners and Williams sit out Wednesday
stories.summary: Tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb and ankle), cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin), and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) did not practice Wednesday. Guard O'Cyrus Torrence also missed for a personal reason. Safeties Cole Bishop, Damar Hamlin and Amani Hooker were limited, and receiver Keon Coleman practiced fully on his ankle.

stories.text: Rookie TJ Parker piles up two sacks and five pressures
stories.summary: The second-round edge rusher sacked Jets quarterback Cade Klubnik twice Sunday, tied for the most among defenders in Week 10. He also logged five pressures. Eleven Buffalo defenders recorded a pressure, and the Bills finished with 18 as a group, sixth most in the league that week.

stories.text: 325: Josh Allen's regular-season touchdowns through 10 seasons
stories.summary: Allen ran for two scores and threw a 45-yard touchdown to DJ Moore against the Jets. That pushed his career total to 325 regular-season touchdowns, the most any player has produced through his first 10 seasons. He passed Peyton Manning, who he had been tied with. Buffalo's 8-1 mark is its best start since 1991.

stories.text: Dolphins visit Buffalo Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The 8-1 Bills host the 1-8 Dolphins at Highmark Stadium. Allen is 14-3 against Miami in his career and has warned teammates the game will not be easy. Watch whether Cook's streak survives a Miami defense that ranks seventh in pass yards allowed and is thin up front.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Kicker job open after three costly misses

stories.text: Dolphins cut kicker Zane Gonzalez after three misses cost seven points
stories.summary: Gonzalez missed field goals from 47 and 51 yards and an extra point in Sunday's 24-22 loss at Indianapolis. Miami lost by two. Coach Jeff Hafley was blunt about the misses, and the team waived Gonzalez on Monday. A replacement had not been named at that point.

stories.text: Willis on injured reserve, Phillips and Biggers worry Hafley
stories.summary: Quarterback Malik Willis went on injured reserve with a groin and core injury. Hafley said no surgery is scheduled but that could change. Defensive linemen Jordan Phillips (arm) and Zeek Biggers (knee) both got hurt Sunday, and Hafley said he has concerns. Center Aaron Brewer also entered the concussion protocol.

stories.text: Rookie Caleb Douglas leads first-year receivers in yards per game
stories.summary: Douglas caught three passes for 71 yards against Indianapolis. He averages 61.2 receiving yards per game, the most among rookie wideouts. He was quarterback Kyle McCord's top target against Colts blitzes, which gives Miami one clear piece to build around.

stories.text: 209: Kyle McCord's passing yards in his first NFL start
stories.summary: McCord went 17 of 32 for 209 yards and ran for a touchdown against the Colts. The yardage is the second most by a Dolphins quarterback in his first start, behind Ryan Tannehill's 219. He also lost a fumble that Indianapolis returned for a touchdown, and Hafley says McCord will start at least three more games.

stories.text: Miami visits Buffalo Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The 1-8 Dolphins have lost three straight and face an 8-1 Bills team that has won five in a row. Miami needs a kicker and protection for McCord, who was sacked three times and hit eight times last week. Watch Phillips, Biggers and Brewer, all listed questionable.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye sidelined indefinitely during bye

stories.text: Maye out indefinitely as Patriots weigh surgery
stories.summary: An AP source says quarterback Drake Maye has a right ankle injury that will keep him out indefinitely, and the team is still deciding whether he needs surgery. Coach Mike Vrabel does not expect Maye back when the team returns from its bye. New England has lost two straight and three of its last four.

stories.text: Maye's ankle reportedly fractured, team has not confirmed
stories.summary: NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Maye fractured his ankle on a first-quarter sack by Aidan Hutchinson in Munich. Vrabel called it a low leg injury and has not confirmed a diagnosis. Maye stayed in Germany for testing and will have more exams back in the U.S. Backup Tommy DeVito and practice squad rookie Behren Morton are the only other quarterbacks on the roster.

stories.text: Corey Kiner leads a backfield that needs a boost
stories.summary: Kiner carried 10 times against Detroit and averages 4.5 yards on 60 carries this year. Rhamondre Stevenson is at 3.7 yards a carry, and TreVeyon Henderson is sidelined after six games. With DeVito likely under center, New England needs Kiner and Stevenson to carry more of the offense.

stories.text: 151: Patriots total yards in Munich, a season low
stories.summary: New England gained 151 yards in the 35-10 loss to the Lions, its lowest total of the season. DeVito went 12 of 24 for 81 yards with a late touchdown to Lan Larison and an interception. The run game added only 61 yards, and DeVito had 19 of them.

stories.text: Bye this week, then the Chargers Nov. 29 at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Patriots are off Sunday and return against the 1-8 Chargers on Nov. 29. The league moved that game out of Sunday night to the 4:05 p.m. ET window on CBS. Watch the quarterback decision: Vrabel has said he is comfortable with DeVito.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Smith says he will play, Glenn waits

stories.text: Smith plans to start in Los Angeles, Glenn wants to see practice
stories.summary: Geno Smith, limping on a left ankle, says he intends to play Sunday at the Chargers. Coach Aaron Glenn will wait to see how the week goes before naming a starter. Imaging showed no serious damage. The Jets are 2-8 with five straight losses and nine quarters without a touchdown. Glenn is 5-22 as head coach.

stories.text: Two rookie receivers miss Wednesday practice, Onyemata window opens
stories.summary: Receivers Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle and hip) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) did not practice, and Harrison Phillips sat out for rest. Smith, Dylan Parham (knee), Joseph Ossai (foot and ankle) and Trevin Wallace (groin) were limited. Defensive lineman David Onyemata's practice window opened after eight weeks on injured reserve.

stories.text: Klubnik moves the offense in relief, then takes three sacks
stories.summary: The fourth-round rookie from Clemson went 11 of 20 for 137 yards with an interception in his debut. His best work was a 10-play, 61-yard drive before halftime that hit Garrett Wilson for 28 and Breece Hall for 11. He ran three times for 26 yards but took three sacks. He starts if Smith cannot go.

stories.text: 37.9%: the Jets' red-zone touchdown rate, last in the NFL
stories.summary: New York has scored touchdowns on fewer than four of every 10 red-zone trips. The offense settled for four Jason Sanders field goals in each of its last two games. It has not scored a touchdown in nine quarters, even though the unit ranks 20th in yards per game.

stories.text: Jets at Chargers Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The 2-8 Jets visit the 1-8 Chargers at SoFi Stadium. Smith, Wallace, Parham, Cooper and cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. are listed questionable. Watch whether New York finally finishes drives against a bad team.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens lean on Brissett with Jackson sidelined

stories.text: Ravens turn to Brissett while Jackson heals from thumb surgery
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson broke and dislocated his thumb on his first snap against Buffalo in Week 8, and coach Jesse Minter said that kind of surgery usually takes 6 to 10 weeks to heal. Baltimore traded for Jacoby Brissett, who threw for 340 yards on 33 of 49 in Monday's 23-20 loss to the Chargers. The Ravens now carry a five-game losing streak into Carolina.

stories.text: Ioane returns to the field and Randall comes off IR
stories.summary: Guard Vega Ioane, a rookie, practiced Wednesday after leaving the Chargers game with a shoulder injury. Rookie running back Adam Randall came off injured reserve and will make his NFL debut Sunday, mainly on returns. Defensive lineman Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) was the one starter not seen on the field.

stories.text: Henry needs more room after 10 carries for 10 yards
stories.summary: Derrick Henry, the oldest active starting running back, averages 69.9 yards per game, 10th in the league, with 699 total yards, ninth. The Chargers held him to 10 yards on 10 carries on Monday night. Baltimore needs a better afternoon from him in Charlotte.

stories.text: 24th: where the Ravens rank in points allowed per game
stories.summary: The Baltimore defense gives up 25.9 points per game, 24th in the NFL. It ranks 12th in yards allowed at 325.4 per game, so the yardage looks fine and the scoreboard does not. The gap between the two numbers is the story.

stories.text: Ravens at Panthers, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Baltimore (4-6) visits first-place Carolina (4-5) at Bank of America Stadium on a short week. Carolina leads the all-time series 4-3, and the teams last met in 2022. Watch whether Brissett and Henry can get the offense moving early.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals ride a five-game win streak to Washington

stories.text: Burrow ties Manning's mark as Bengals win five straight
stories.summary: Joe Burrow has thrown or run for at least four touchdowns in five straight games, tying Peyton Manning's 2004 run for the longest streak in NFL history. He went 35 of 44 for 406 yards and four scores in the 38-18 win over Pittsburgh. Cincinnati sits alone atop the AFC North at 7-2.

stories.text: Four Bengals listed questionable for Monday night
stories.summary: Safety Kyle Dugger, tackle Myles Hinton, linebacker Oren Burks and guard Dalton Risner carry questionable tags in SI's injury rundown for the Commanders game. Receiver Andrei Iosivas remains on injured reserve with a designation to return. The team's official Friday report will settle the final statuses.

stories.text: Chase Brown scores twice as a receiver against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Running back Chase Brown caught eight passes for 39 yards and two touchdowns, from 2 and 4 yards, against the Steelers. He also ran 10 times for 44 yards. Brown has 441 rushing yards this season.

stories.text: 21: completions Cincinnati made before Pittsburgh's first
stories.summary: The Bengals completed 21 passes before the Steelers completed one, which ties the most by one team before an opponent's first since play-by-play records began in 1978. Burrow went 26 of 34 for 302 yards and three touchdowns in the first half alone. Cincinnati led 24-3 at the break.

stories.text: Bengals at Commanders, Monday at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Cincinnati (7-2) visits Northwest Stadium to face Washington (3-5-1). The Bengals rank first in passing offense at 298.8 yards per game and second in third-down offense. Washington ranks 31st against the pass, allowing 244.8 yards per game.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns take a 6-4 record into the bye

stories.text: Browns are the first team to win six games by four or fewer
stories.summary: All six Cleveland wins this season have come by four points or fewer, a first in NFL history. The Browns rallied from 17-0 down to beat Houston 27-24, their fourth double-digit comeback win, a franchise record. They hold the last AFC wild-card spot at 6-4 under first-year coach Todd Monken.

stories.text: Barnett's hamstring and Boston's toe get bye-week time
stories.summary: Defensive end Derek Barnett strained a hamstring in the first quarter against Houston. Receiver Denzel Boston is playing through a nagging toe injury. The bye gives both extra days before the Raiders visit on Nov. 29.

stories.text: Watson strings together three straight 300-yard games
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson threw for 312 yards and ran for another 49 and a touchdown against Houston. He is the first Browns quarterback with three straight 300-yard games since Joe Flacco in 2023. Watson has 2,118 passing yards, 7 touchdowns and 4 interceptions this season, and he is 4-0 at home.

stories.text: 78-13: how badly Cleveland trails in the first quarter
stories.summary: Opponents have outscored the Browns 78-13 in the first 15 minutes of games. Cleveland is the only team in the league that has not scored on an opening drive, and its defense has allowed points on the first possession in eight of 10 games. The slow starts explain the comebacks.

stories.text: Bye now, then Raiders on Sunday Night Football Nov. 29
stories.summary: Cleveland is off this week, then hosts Las Vegas (4-6) on Nov. 29 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC after the NFL flexed the game into prime time. It is the Browns' first Sunday Night Football game since 2021. Three straight home games follow the bye, and the Browns close the season against Cincinnati on Jan. 10.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers look to bounce back in Philadelphia

stories.text: Steelers try to shake off a 38-18 loss against 2-7 Eagles
stories.summary: Pittsburgh fell behind 24-3 at halftime in Cincinnati, and Aaron Rodgers finished 15 of 29 for 143 yards with two late touchdowns. The loss dropped the Steelers to 6-3 and out of first place in the AFC North. They now visit a Philadelphia team that is 2-7.

stories.text: Watt, Heyward and Washington go full after rest days
stories.summary: T.J. Watt, Cameron Heyward and tight end Darnell Washington sat out Wednesday with rest designations and practiced fully Thursday. Linebacker Patrick Queen (hand) was limited both days, and linebacker Nick Herbig (hip, ribs) did not practice either day. Receivers Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson have their 21-day practice windows open while on injured reserve.

stories.text: Warren leads the Steelers with 719 rushing yards
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren has 719 rushing yards on 126 carries, 5.7 per attempt, plus 30 catches for 320 yards. Pittsburgh ranks fourth in the league, tied, at 4.8 yards per carry. Cincinnati held him to 41 yards from scrimmage on seven carries.

stories.text: 83.2: rushing yards allowed per game, third in the NFL
stories.summary: The Steelers allow 83.2 rushing yards per game, third in the league, and they have 27 sacks, tied for fifth. Pittsburgh is 4-0 at home and 2-3 on the road. Philadelphia is another road game, and the defense gave up 38 points in Cincinnati last Sunday.

stories.text: Steelers at Eagles, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh (6-3) plays at Lincoln Financial Field against a 2-7 Eagles team in Mike McCarthy's first season as head coach. Watt has 7.5 sacks and a pick-six this season. Watch whether Rodgers, who has been sacked 26 times, gets time to throw.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans rout Colts 26-3 and climb to 4-6

stories.text: Texans blow out Colts 26-3 on Thursday night
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game, and the defense gave up three points. Houston has won four of its last six after an 0-4 start. ESPN Analytics puts its playoff chance at 38 percent.

stories.text: Woody Marks sits with a concussion, Montgomery returns
stories.summary: Running back Woody Marks missed the Colts game with a concussion. David Montgomery came back from the groin injury he suffered in Week 5 and carried 26 times for 107 yards, his best game since Week 1.

stories.text: Will Anderson Jr. gets first career safety, leads NFL in sacks
stories.summary: Anderson sacked Daniel Jones in the end zone for the first safety of his career. He finished with seven pressures and four quarterback hits. He now has 11.5 sacks, the most in the league.

stories.text: 167: Total yards the Colts gathered against Houston
stories.summary: The Texans defense allowed three points and 167 yards. Indianapolis did not score a touchdown, and Dominique Robinson blocked a field goal. Cornerback Kamari Lassiter intercepted a pass and allowed no catches on six targets, per Next Gen Stats.

stories.text: Ravens come to Houston Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Houston plays Baltimore at home on CBS after a ten-day break. Watch whether the pass rush that cracked Indianapolis can keep up that pressure against a different kind of offense. Houston needs the win to stay in the playoff chase.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts get no touchdown and fall to 3-8

stories.text: Colts lose 26-3 and fail to reach the end zone
stories.summary: Indianapolis scored on its opening drive, then did not score again until the fourth quarter. It was the first game this season without a touchdown. The Colts are 3-8.

stories.text: Both starting tackles sit, McGowan leaves with hamstring
stories.summary: Bernhard Raimann (concussion) and Jalen Travis (knee) were inactive, as were cornerbacks Sauce Gardner (calf) and Charvarius Ward (knee). Running back Seth McGowan hurt a hamstring late in the second quarter and did not return.

stories.text: Daniel Jones struggles behind a patched line
stories.summary: Jones completed 12 of 27 passes for 144 yards with one interception, a 45.9 passer rating. Anthony Richardson entered midway through the fourth quarter and went 0 for 2 as a passer.

stories.text: 1.9: Jonathan Taylor's yards per carry against Houston
stories.summary: Taylor's average was the second lowest of his career. The Colts have also allowed 608 rushing yards over their last four games, 151.8 per game.

stories.text: Giants visit Indianapolis Sunday, Nov. 29 at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: The Colts host New York on Fox after a ten-day break, with time to get tackles Raimann and Travis and corners Gardner and Ward healthy. Watch whether the run defense tightens up against a Giants offense that leans on Cam Skattebo.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Bates and Davis set to debut at the Giants

stories.text: Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis expected to debut Sunday
stories.summary: Both players came over before the Nov. 10 trade deadline and used the bye week to learn the defense. Coordinator Anthony Campanile said he is fired up to add them. He also wants cleaner tackling after the 40-23 win over Tennessee.

stories.text: Tuten drops to no practice Thursday, Hainsey out
stories.summary: Running back Bhayshul Tuten went from limited Wednesday to a non-participant Thursday with a foot issue. He has played the last two games on little practice. Center Robert Hainsey missed again with a knee injury, and Jonah Monheim is set to start. Eleven players carried a designation.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence chases a fifth straight 30-point game
stories.summary: Lawrence threw for a season-high 352 yards against Tennessee. He has 2,284 yards, 21 touchdowns and five interceptions through nine games. Jacksonville is going after a franchise-record fifth straight game with 30 points.

stories.text: +125: Jacksonville's point differential, best in the NFL
stories.summary: The Jaguars also lead the league with a plus-9 turnover margin. They are off to their best nine-game start since 1999.

stories.text: At the Giants Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Jacksonville (7-2) visits New York (5-3-1) at MetLife Stadium. Coach Liam Coen says the game will be won in the trenches, with a backup center on one side and Abdul Carter and the Giants pass rush on the other. The Titans come to Jacksonville on Nov. 29.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans head to Dallas for the first time since 2018

stories.text: Titans visit AT&T Stadium for the first time since 2018
stories.summary: Tennessee (1-8) comes off a 40-23 loss to Jacksonville in which it was outscored 10-0 late. Dallas is 4-6 and still chasing the NFC East. The Cowboys lead the series 9-7.

stories.text: Spears and Adams return to limited work, Tate still limited
stories.summary: Running back Tyjae Spears (knee) and safety Tony Adams (concussion) moved from no practice Wednesday to limited Thursday. Receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder) was limited both days. Tony Pollard sat Thursday for rest, not injury.

stories.text: Cam Ward piles up yards through the air and on the ground
stories.summary: Ward is 54 of 79 for 535 yards, four touchdowns and one interception over his last two games. He also ran for 80 yards on 10 carries in that span.

stories.text: 7.5: Jacob Martin's career-high sack total
stories.summary: Martin's 7.5 sacks tie him for seventh in the NFL this season. Kicker Joey Slye also hit from 53, 54 and 50 yards against Jacksonville, tying the club record for a game.

stories.text: At Dallas Sunday, noon CT on Fox
stories.summary: Kickoff is 1 p.m. ET. The Titans face a Cowboys passing offense that ranks third in the NFL at 265.5 yards per game, led by Dak Prescott's 2,724 yards and 21 touchdowns. Tennessee then visits Jacksonville on Nov. 29.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos return from the bye with a record streak

stories.text: Broncos stretch their one-score win streak to an NFL record 16
stories.summary: Denver beat Carolina 26-21 on Nov. 8 after Nik Bonitto stripped Bryce Young and the Broncos recovered at their own 44 with under 90 seconds left. Bo Nix sealed it with a one-yard sneak three plays later. The 16th straight one-score win passed the Colts' mark of 15, and the Broncos have had a bye to rest since.

stories.text: Brandon Jones is the only Broncos name still limited twice
stories.summary: Safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday and Thursday. Wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and cornerback Riley Moss (both concussions), safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) and tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) were full participants both days. Cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine moved from limited to full Thursday. No game designations are out yet.

stories.text: Bonitto leads a Denver pass rush that sits top 10 in sacks
stories.summary: Nik Bonitto has 4.5 sacks and 6.5 tackles for loss, and the Broncos rank in the top 10 with 26 sacks and 104 quarterback pressures. Patrick Surtain has held opposing receivers under nine yards per catch even though he missed three games. Rookie Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders see that front on Sunday.

stories.text: 355.0: yards per game Denver allows, 27th in the NFL
stories.summary: The yardage hides how well the Broncos defend the scoreboard. They allow 20.7 points per game, ninth in the league, because the pass rush ends drives early. The gap between yards and points is the story to watch against a Raiders offense that takes sacks.

stories.text: Raiders visit Empower Field on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Denver (7-2) hosts Las Vegas (4-6) in an AFC West game. Watch whether Waddle and Moss clear the concussion protocol to play, and how a rookie quarterback handles the Broncos rush a second week in a row.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs plan a patchwork line against Arizona

stories.text: Chiefs expect Ezeudu and Caliendo to start on a rebuilt line
stories.summary: Right guard Trey Smith remains in the concussion protocol and right tackle Jaylon Moore is still out of practice with an ankle injury. Andy Reid's staff expects Josh Ezeudu and Mike Caliendo to start in their place against Arizona. Running back Kenneth Walker III also missed Wednesday with a groin injury that Reid called day-to-day.

stories.text: Walker, Moore and Smith sit out again on Thursday
stories.summary: Kenneth Walker III (groin), Jaylon Moore (ankle) and Trey Smith (concussion) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Travis Kelce (calf and ankle), Patrick Mahomes (knee and right elbow), Rashee Rice (knee) and Nick Bolton (shin, full Thursday) all practiced fully on Thursday. Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was limited both days.

stories.text: Mahomes has 10 touchdown passes and no picks in three games
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes has thrown for 2,385 yards, 19 touchdowns and four interceptions this season, per FOX Sports, with 10 of those scores coming in his last three games. His five-touchdown, 348-yard day in Atlanta was his first five-score game since September 2022. He still carries a knee and right elbow note on the practice report, and he practiced fully both days.

stories.text: 35: points the Chiefs scored in each of their last two wins
stories.summary: Kansas City beat the Jets 35-12 and then the Falcons 35-13 in Atlanta. Mahomes threw no interceptions across that stretch. The offense now faces a Cardinals team that SI reports has not scored a touchdown since its 33-30 win in Dallas to open the month.

stories.text: Cardinals visit Arrowhead on Sunday at 1 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Kansas City (7-2) hosts Arizona (3-7). Watch the right side of the offensive line and whether Walker plays or Emmett Johnson carries the load.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Mendoza faces a second top defense in Denver

stories.text: Mendoza gets a second straight test against a top defense
stories.summary: In his first start against Seattle, Fernando Mendoza went 11 of 13 for 90 yards with a 10-yard rushing touchdown in the first half. The offense then cooled, gained no positive yardage in the third quarter, and Mendoza took six sacks in the 21-13 loss. Denver's pass rush ranks in the top 10 in sacks and pressures.

stories.text: Zuhn, Hemingway and Gay miss Thursday's practice
stories.summary: Right guard Trey Zuhn (illness), defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and kicker Matt Gay (hip) did not practice Thursday. Tight end Brock Bowers (ankle and quad) went from no practice Wednesday to limited Thursday. Defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) also sat out Thursday. No game designations are out yet.

stories.text: Crosby sits half a sack from 75 for his career
stories.summary: Maxx Crosby needs 0.5 sacks to reach 75.0 for his career, a mark the Raiders' game preview ties to undrafted or late-round players. He lines up against a Denver front with 26 sacks. Running back Ashton Jeanty is also one receiving touchdown from a franchise milestone for backs over a 27-game span.

stories.text: 70.7: rushing yards per game, the Raiders' weak spot
stories.summary: Las Vegas throws for 243.5 yards per game but runs for just 70.7, per FOX Sports team stats. The Raiders score 25.1 points per game and allow 28.9, so the passing game carries the offense.

stories.text: Raiders visit Denver on Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Las Vegas (4-6) faces the 7-2 Broncos at Empower Field. Denver won the last two meetings, 10-7 and 24-17. Watch Bowers' ankle and whether the Raiders can protect Mendoza.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers join a short list of 0-8 Monday winners

stories.text: Chargers become the second team to win on MNF after an 0-8 start
stories.summary: Los Angeles beat Baltimore 23-20 on Monday to end an eight-game winless start. ESPN Insights says only the 2013 Buccaneers had won a Monday night game after starting 0-8 or worse. The Chargers led 17-10 at halftime and held on after a late Zay Flowers fumble.

stories.text: McConkey limited with a back issue on Thursday
stories.summary: Wide receiver Ladd McConkey was a limited participant Thursday because of a back problem. Jets quarterback Geno Smith (ankle) was limited and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle and hip) did not practice.

stories.text: Hampton posts a season-high 105 yards in the first win
stories.summary: Omarion Hampton ran for a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown against Baltimore and averages 4.8 yards per carry this season. He has four rushing touchdowns and 474 yards through nine games. Jets coach Aaron Glenn said the Chargers are feeling good about themselves.

stories.text: 2: sacks Herbert took, against nearly four per game
stories.summary: Justin Herbert went down only twice against Baltimore, well below his average of nearly four sacks a game over the first eight weeks. The Chargers also outrushed the Ravens 160-16, and Tarheeb Still forced the Flowers fumble that Elijah Molden recovered with 2:03 left.

stories.text: Jets visit SoFi Stadium on Sunday at 4:05 PM ET on Fox
stories.summary: Los Angeles (1-8) hosts New York (2-8) and looks for its first back-to-back wins. Watch whether Hampton keeps the run game going and how McConkey's back holds up.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Prescott backs Pettine switch as Titans arrive

stories.text: Prescott calls Pettine move a business decision
stories.summary: Dak Prescott told reporters Thursday that Dallas should accept Brian Schottenheimer's call to hand defensive play-calling to Mike Pettine. Christian Parker stays on as coordinator. Prescott said he would not question the defense's effort and wants the room focused on Tennessee, not on what the schedule looks like after Sunday.

stories.text: Bland and Booker out, Ferguson still not practicing
stories.summary: Cornerback DaRon Bland (ankle), guard Tyler Booker (ankle) and tight end Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Safety P.J. Locke (concussion) and receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) also sat both days. Linebacker Von Miller returned to full work Thursday after a rest day.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb nears 1,000 yards with 976 through 10 games
stories.summary: Lamb has 77 catches, 976 yards and 8 touchdowns heading into Week 11. George Pickens adds 678 yards and 5 touchdowns, and Dallas has the No. 3 passing offense in the league. The pair gives Prescott two receivers who command attention on every down.

stories.text: 28.6 to 28.2: Dallas scores and allows nearly the same
stories.summary: The Cowboys average 28.6 points per game and give up 28.2. Dak Prescott has 2,724 passing yards, third in the NFL, and 21 touchdowns, tied for third. The offense keeps Dallas in every game, and the defense keeps it from winning them.

stories.text: Titans visit AT&T Stadium Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee is 1-8 and has lost three straight, including a 40-23 home loss to Jacksonville. The Titans have not played at AT&T Stadium since a 28-14 win on Nov. 5, 2018. Dallas then faces Philadelphia, and the Cowboys' next two opponents have three wins combined.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants meet their first winning team of 2026

stories.text: Giants face first winning opponent while chasing NFC East
stories.summary: The 5-3-1 Giants lead the division and have not finished first in it in 15 years. Jacksonville is 7-2 and the first team with a winning record on New York's schedule. The Jaguars have a +125 point differential and lead the league in turnover margin at +9.

stories.text: Harrison and Pinnock back to full, Nic Jones still out
stories.summary: Linebacker Malik Harrison (groin) and safety Jason Pinnock (hip) moved from limited Wednesday to full Thursday. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) and Deonte Banks (shoulder) practiced fully both days. Cornerback Nic Jones (knee) did not practice either day.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely turns 11 targets into 127 yards
stories.summary: Likely caught 9 of 11 targets for 127 yards and a touchdown in the 24-21 loss at Washington. In J.J. McCarthy's three starts, he has 16 catches for 192 yards and 2 touchdowns on 21 targets. Cam Skattebo has 202 rushing yards on 35 carries in McCarthy's last two starts.

stories.text: 17: fumbles by the Giants offense in nine games
stories.summary: That works out to about 1.9 per game and ties New York with the Chargers for the most in the league. Jacksonville leads the NFL in turnover margin, so ball security decides this one early. The Giants also blitz on 40.6% of passing snaps, a rate only three teams top.

stories.text: Jaguars visit MetLife Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: The league moved the game from the 1:00 PM slot into the late CBS window. Trevor Lawrence is the league leader in yards per attempt and passer rating when he faces no blitz, which sets up the Giants' pressure packages. Jacksonville is 7-2 and New York is 5-3-1.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles add Ertz and look to end a seven-game skid

stories.text: Eagles activate Zach Ertz and carry five tight ends
stories.summary: Philadelphia moved Ertz from the practice squad to the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's Steelers game. He joins Dallas Goedert, Grant Calcaterra, Johnny Mundt and rookie Eli Stowers. Nick Sirianni confirmed Joe Milton will make his second start and Sean Mannion will keep calling plays.

stories.text: Smith practices fully Thursday, Baun sits with a back issue
stories.summary: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) went from limited Wednesday to full Thursday. Linebackers Zack Baun (back) and Smael Mondon (ankle) did not practice. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was limited, and Saquon Barkley (hamstring) practiced fully.

stories.text: Makai Lemon carries the receiver room with 312 yards
stories.summary: The rookie receiver has 37 catches for 312 yards and one touchdown in nine games. He has been the steady target while Smith missed time with a hamstring injury. Smith practiced fully Thursday and could return Sunday.

stories.text: 1: time the Eagles topped 300 yards in four games without Smith
stories.summary: Philadelphia has reached 200 passing yards only once in that stretch. The Eagles are 2-7 and have lost seven straight, and they have not won since Smith left the lineup. Smith blames self-inflicted errors such as missed assignments, not his absence alone.

stories.text: Steelers visit the Linc Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is 6-3 and second in the AFC North after a 38-18 loss to Cincinnati. It is the Eagles' Salute to Service game. Philadelphia carries the NFL's longest active losing streak at seven games.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders seek a third straight win over Cincinnati

stories.text: Commanders chase a third straight win over Bengals
stories.summary: Washington has beaten Cincinnati in its last three meetings. A win Monday would give the franchise three straight over the Bengals for the first time. Jayden Daniels said the focus is scoring points against a Cincinnati offense that ranks third in points per game.

stories.text: Daniels, Okonkwo and Croskey-Merritt all practice fully
stories.summary: Daniels (left elbow), tight end Chig Okonkwo (back) and running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) all had full practice Thursday. Stefon Diggs took a rest day, and safety Quan Martin (shoulder) was limited. Cincinnati's Joe Burrow also practiced fully while listed with an illness.

stories.text: Sonny Styles leads Washington with 80 tackles
stories.summary: The linebacker has the most tackles on the team. Odafe Oweh leads the Commanders with 5 sacks, and cornerback Rasul Douglas has 3 interceptions. Styles will spend Monday night chasing Chase Brown and Cincinnati's quick passing game.

stories.text: +7: Washington's turnover margin, tied for third in the NFL
stories.summary: The Commanders take the ball away more often than they give it up, even at 3-5-1. Cincinnati's margin is +2. Daniels threw two interceptions in the win over the Giants, so the edge is not automatic.

stories.text: Bengals visit Monday night, 8:15 PM ET on ESPN
stories.summary: Cincinnati is 7-2 and brings the top passing offense in the league at 298.8 yards per game and the second-best third-down rate at 51.9%. Washington's defense allows 39.3% on third down, 15th in the league. The game is at Northwest Stadium on Nov. 23.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears chase a fifth straight win over the Saints

stories.text: Bears put a four-game win streak on the line against the Saints
stories.summary: Chicago (7-2) comes out of its bye with four straight wins, including a road win in Seattle. New Orleans (3-6) lost 20-17 to Carolina last week and allows 26.2 points per game. The Bears host the Saints on Sunday at Soldier Field.

stories.text: Odeyingbo stays on IR as Burden clears the concussion protocol
stories.summary: Receiver Luther Burden III has exited the concussion protocol, though Ben Johnson said his Week 11 status is still to be determined. Running back Kyle Monangai (toe) and cornerback Malik Muhammad II are on track to play. Cornerback Kyler Gordon (shoulder) is day-to-day, and defensive lineman Dayo Odeyingbo will not be activated from injured reserve this week.

stories.text: Williams says four-interception game will not make him cautious
stories.summary: Caleb Williams threw a career-high four interceptions in the 27-24 win over Tampa Bay on Nov. 8, then led the drive for Cairo Santos' 38-yard winning field goal. Tampa Bay blitzed him on 66 percent of his dropbacks. Williams said he got greedy on one goal-line throw and that he will keep attacking.

stories.text: 26.2: points per game the Saints give up
stories.summary: New Orleans also allows 231 passing yards per game. Williams went 22 of 37 for 279 yards, two touchdowns and four interceptions in his last start. Against the Saints last season he went 15 of 26 for 172 yards with one interception.

stories.text: Saints visit Soldier Field Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Chicago (7-2) hosts New Orleans (3-6) in Week 11. The Saints list center Erik McCoy and tackle Taliese Fuaga as doubtful. Watch whether the Bears protect Williams against pressure without extra blockers.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions defense tightens during a five-game win streak

stories.text: Lions share the NFC North lead and ask the defense to hold
stories.summary: Detroit (7-2) wins on tiebreakers over Chicago and Minnesota, who are also 7-2. The Lions gave up 31.8 points per game in a 2-2 start and 14.4 per game during the five-game win streak. They are 5-0 at Ford Field.

stories.text: Linebacker Campbell and Hutchinson are out, Branch is back
stories.summary: Edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL and linebacker Jack Campbell, the team's leading tackler, is out for the season. Safety Brian Branch returned from injured reserve, and safety Kerby Joseph may return soon. Detroit has to replace both from a defense that had improved over the last five games.

stories.text: McNeill leads the Lions with 6.5 sacks
stories.summary: Defensive lineman Alim McNeill leads Detroit with 6.5 sacks, and linebacker Derrick Barnes has 40 tackles and 3.0 sacks. With Hutchinson down, the interior pass rush matters more. The Lions have 32.0 sacks, third most in the league.

stories.text: 21: takeaways by Tampa Bay, the most in the NFL
stories.summary: The Buccaneers also lead the league with 16 interceptions. Detroit has the third-best offense and the fifth-best run defense, according to the Bucs' preview. Jared Goff needs a clean day against that ball-hawking secondary.

stories.text: Buccaneers visit Ford Field Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Detroit (7-2) hosts Tampa Bay (3-6). Tampa Bay has won three of the last four games at Ford Field. Quarterback Baker Mayfield did not practice Wednesday, so his status is worth watching.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers keep their coaches, search for pass protection

stories.text: LaFleur keeps his staff after the eight-sack loss
stories.summary: Matt LaFleur said he will make no staff changes, so coordinator Adam Stenavich and line coach Luke Butkus stay. He said the pass protection was as bad as it looked live. Green Bay (6-4) lost 30-10 to Minnesota and now has a short week before the Rams.

stories.text: Cisse, Melton and Moore are bye-week watch items
stories.summary: Rookie cornerback Brandon Cisse hurt his ribs against Minnesota, and LaFleur does not expect him to miss significant time. LaFleur is not worried about Bo Melton (thigh), while Skyy Moore (ankle) needs more evaluation. Moore and Melton both return kicks.

stories.text: Love absorbs eight sacks and four turnovers
stories.summary: Jordan Love took eight sacks as Green Bay turned the ball over four times in the 30-10 loss. Minnesota's rushers jumped the snap, and the Packers fell behind 20-0 early. Across two games against the Vikings, Love was sacked 12 times and hit 27 times.

stories.text: 31%: Green Bay's pass block win rate, worst since 2017
stories.summary: TSN, citing ESPN's tracking, says Green Bay is on pace for the lowest pass block win rate since the metric began in 2017. The Packers have started four different left guards and seven guards this season. Their run game ranks last in the NFL in yards per game.

stories.text: At the Rams Wednesday, Nov. 25, at 8 p.m. ET on Netflix
stories.summary: Green Bay is on a bye this week and plays the first Thanksgiving Eve game. LaFleur wants Micah Parsons to make his season debut, but Parsons must be activated from the PUP list first. Guard Kevin Zeitler and center Sean Rhyan could return to the line.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings trained at simulated altitude for Mexico City

stories.text: Vikings spent five weeks training for Mexico City altitude
stories.summary: Minnesota used a room that simulates 12,000 feet, logging nearly 450 sessions. Players built up from a simulated 9,000 feet, and the team will fly out Saturday to avoid the first days at elevation. Supplemental oxygen will be on the sideline and in the locker room at halftime.

stories.text: Addison and Murray did not practice, Hockenson was limited
stories.summary: Receiver Jordan Addison (thumb) and quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Tight end T.J. Hockenson (wrist) was limited both days, while receiver Jauan Jennings (calf) and linebacker Blake Cashman (concussion) practiced fully. Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers (quad) was added Thursday as limited.

stories.text: Bartholomew sets career highs with Hockenson out
stories.summary: Tight end Gavin Bartholomew caught a touchdown from Kirk Cousins, his first in nine career games, and set career highs with 36 yards on three catches and 53 snaps. Next Gen Stats credited him 7 yards after the catch over expected. He also threw a lead block on a 3-yard screen.

stories.text: 8: sacks by Minnesota, the most since Dec. 16, 2018
stories.summary: The Vikings hit Jordan Love eight times at Lambeau Field in the 30-10 win. Dallas Turner's eighth sack of the season matched his 2025 total. Minnesota finished plus-three in turnover margin.

stories.text: At the 49ers in Mexico City Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Minnesota visits San Francisco (8-1) at Estadio Banorte. It is the Vikings' first game in Mexico, and the all-time series is tied 25-25-1. Watch how Cousins handles the altitude and the 49ers' pass rush.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Rees keeps the playbook as the bye begins

stories.text: Stefanski keeps Rees as play caller through the bye
stories.summary: Kevin Stefanski confirmed that Tommy Rees will keep calling plays, but he would not state his confidence in him. The staff will review the whole offense during the bye. Stefanski said the team needs to look at its process after four straight three-and-outs to open the loss to Kansas City.

stories.text: London's concussion symptoms should clear by the Vikings game
stories.summary: Drake London is dealing with concussion symptoms, but ClutchPoints reports he is expected to be ready for the Nov. 29 trip to Minnesota. The bye gives him extra time to recover before the Falcons return to practice.

stories.text: Kendal Daniels leads the defense with 69 tackles
stories.summary: With Jessie Bates III traded to Jacksonville, linebacker Kendal Daniels is the Falcons' leading tackler at 69. ClutchPoints argues he should direct the defense as coordinator Jeff Ulbrich rebuilds the back end.

stories.text: 51-of-98: Penix's line over the last three games
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. has thrown for 573 yards, one touchdown and six interceptions in his last three starts. The offense has scored 30 points in that span and averaged 304.3 yards per game. Atlanta led the NFL in scoring through his first five starts.

stories.text: Bye now, then Sunday, Nov. 29 at the 1 p.m. Vikings game
stories.summary: Atlanta rests this week and returns for a 1 p.m. ET game at Minnesota on FOX. The Falcons are 3-7 and sit 1.5 games behind first-place Carolina in the NFC South, with seven games left.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Canales wants the flags gone before Ravens

stories.text: Canales wants the penalties gone after a franchise-record 17
stories.summary: Carolina beat New Orleans 20-17 and took sole possession of first place, but it drew 17 flags for 152 yards, a franchise record. Dave Canales said the team must cut the mistakes it controls, naming offsides, pre-snap infractions and delay of game.

stories.text: Both tight ends sit with knee issues, Young practices in full
stories.summary: Tommy Tremble and Darren Waller did not practice Wednesday with knee injuries, and Canales called both a concern. Bryce Young took every rep after foot soreness from the Saints game. Bobby Okereke (foot) has missed two weeks, and Will Lee III returned in full.

stories.text: Ryan Fitzgerald ends the Saints game from 54 yards
stories.summary: Ryan Fitzgerald hit a 54-yard field goal as time expired to give Carolina its 20-17 win. A 30-yard pass interference call on Kool-Aid McKinstry put the Panthers in range for the kick.

stories.text: 280: yards Young hit in each of the first five games, not since
stories.summary: Bryce Young passed for at least 280 yards in each of Carolina's first five games and has not reached that mark in the last four. He went 17-of-30 for 200 yards against New Orleans, with no touchdowns and no interceptions.

stories.text: Ravens visit Charlotte Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Carolina (4-5) hosts Baltimore (4-6) at Bank of America Stadium. Lamar Jackson is on injured reserve for the Ravens. Watch whether the Panthers can keep first place without another penalty pile.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints meet ex-coach Allen in Chicago

stories.text: Saints face old coach Dennis Allen at Soldier Field
stories.summary: New Orleans opens a two-game road trip against division leaders at Chicago. Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen coached the Saints from 2022 to 2024. The Saints also need to gain ground in the NFC South after the Week 10 loss in Carolina.

stories.text: Seven Saints did not practice Wednesday, including McCoy and Fuaga
stories.summary: Cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion), tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), center Erik McCoy (biceps), tackle Asim Richards (knee) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) sat out. Alvin Kamara had a rest day and Justin Reid missed for a personal matter.

stories.text: Rookie Jordyn Tyson catches 11 passes for 80 yards
stories.summary: Receiver Jordyn Tyson had the most catches by a Saints rookie in a game since Pierre Thomas, per the team. He was limited Wednesday with a chest injury.

stories.text: -8: the Saints' turnover margin, 29th in the NFL
stories.summary: New Orleans also ranks 29th in total defense at 360.8 yards per game and 26th in rushing offense at 90.1. Against Carolina, Tyler Shough threw an interception and lost a fumble.

stories.text: Saints visit the 7-2 Bears Sunday at noon CT on FOX
stories.summary: Kickoff is 12 p.m. CT (1 p.m. ET) at Soldier Field, and Chicago returns from its Week 10 bye. The Saints lead the all-time regular-season series 18-14, but Chicago won the last meeting 26-14 in 2025.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Mayfield's foot clouds Detroit trip

stories.text: Mayfield's foot strain points toward Daniels starting
stories.summary: Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield has a foot strain from the last game before the bye and that the Bucs are trending toward rookie Jalon Daniels. Daniels is 1-2 in three starts this season, and Rapoport said not to rule Mayfield out.

stories.text: Mayfield and Winfield miss practice, Diaby limited
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield (foot, right thumb) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle) did not practice Wednesday. Edge rusher Yaya Diaby (knee) was limited. Tristan Wirfs, Cade Otton and Josh Hayes all practiced in full.

stories.text: Rookie Keionte Scott leads defensive backs with five pressures
stories.summary: The slot defender has five quarterback pressures, the most among NFL defensive backs. He draws Amon-Ra St. Brown (65 catches, 755 yards) in Detroit.

stories.text: 163.9: rushing yards per game, tops in the NFL
stories.summary: Tampa Bay leads the league in rushing offense and in rushing defense at 79.1 yards allowed per game. The Bucs also lead the NFL with 21 takeaways, 16 of them interceptions.

stories.text: Bucs visit the 7-2 Lions Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tampa Bay (3-6) plays at Ford Field and needs a win to avoid falling two games behind Carolina. Detroit has won five straight, and Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards and touchdowns.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Cardinals draw a hot Mahomes at Arrowhead

stories.text: Cardinals draw a Mahomes who has not thrown an interception in three games
stories.summary: Patrick Mahomes threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns in Kansas City's 35-13 win at Atlanta. He has 10 touchdown passes and no interceptions over his last three games. Arizona (3-7) has not scored a touchdown since its 33-30 win over Dallas and now faces that passing game on the road.

stories.text: Cardinals line goes limited as Baker and Sweat rest
stories.summary: Safety Budda Baker, guard Isaac Seumalo, edge rusher Josh Sweat and linebacker Mack Wilson sat out Wednesday for rest, and lineman Walter Nolen missed with an illness. The bigger concern is up front. Center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion), guard Jon Gaines (ankle) and tackle Jayden Williams (knee) all practiced in a limited role. Defensive lineman Jordan Burch hurt his knee against the Rams and did not return.

stories.text: Carson Beck inherits the job after two quarterback moves
stories.summary: Beck, a third-round pick out of Miami, started against the Rams after Arizona traded Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore on Nov. 6 and Gardner Minshew went down with a season-ending elbow injury. The rookie finished 11 of 18 for 108 yards with two interceptions. Kansas City is his second NFL start.

stories.text: 123: Total yards the Cardinals gathered against the Rams
stories.summary: Arizona held a 6-3 lead late in the second quarter, then gained only 123 yards in the 34-6 loss, most of them after the game was decided. The Cardinals have also lost 11 straight home games, a streak of 427 days. The league record is 14.

stories.text: Cardinals at Chiefs Sunday, 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Arizona (3-7) travels to Arrowhead Stadium to face Kansas City (7-2) on Sunday, Nov. 22. CBS has the game and Paramount+ streams it. Watch whether the Cardinals protect Beck with a patchwork line and finally find the end zone.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams use the bye to sort out their center spot

stories.text: Rams lost both centers against Arizona and need the bye to sort it out
stories.summary: Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and Dylan McMahon (knee) both left the 34-6 win in the first half, and Beaux Limmer slid over to center. The Rams are 6-4 with four straight wins and off this week. Protecting Matthew Stafford up the middle is the first order of business before Green Bay.

stories.text: McVay sets Dec. 3 as a realistic date for Davante Adams
stories.summary: On Nov. 11, Sean McVay said he expects Adams to miss two more games and return against Kansas City on Dec. 3. Puka Nacua is out with a knee injury and the team hopes to have him back in December. Receiver Jordan Whittington is on injured reserve with a back injury, and tight end Terrance Ferguson is out indefinitely with a re-injured hamstring.

stories.text: Blake Corum runs for 100 yards against Arizona
stories.summary: Corum ran for 100 yards and scored on a 1-yard touchdown as the Rams pulled away from the Cardinals. With the receiver group thin, the ground game carried more of the load. Stafford added 249 yards and three touchdown passes.

stories.text: 1:06: How little time the Rams needed for two scores before halftime
stories.summary: Los Angeles trailed 6-3 late in the second quarter. The Rams then scored twice in the final 1:06 of the half and led 17-6 at the break. Arizona never got closer in the 34-6 loss.

stories.text: Rams host Packers Wednesday, 8 p.m. ET on Netflix
stories.summary: Los Angeles is on its bye this week, then plays Green Bay at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 25, the first NFL game on Thanksgiving Eve. Netflix streams it. Watch how many of the injured receivers and linemen the Rams get back on a short turnaround.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: McCaffrey's big day sets up the Mexico City trip

stories.text: McCaffrey's 223 yards carry the 49ers to 8-1
stories.summary: Christian McCaffrey had a career-best 161 receiving yards and 62 rushing yards in the 46-40 win at Dallas. He scored on catches of 74 and 66 yards and added a 16-yard touchdown. San Francisco gained 584 yards, the fifth most in franchise history, and now heads to Mexico City.

stories.text: Evans misses another practice with Achilles tendinitis
stories.summary: Mike Evans did not practice Wednesday and has missed three straight games. Kyle Shanahan said the team is taking it day by day. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw (neck) also sat out, and cornerback Renardo Green (back) was limited after he left the Dallas game. Safeties Ji'Ayir Brown and Siran Neal, end Khalid Kareem and cornerback Upton Stout were also limited.

stories.text: Deebo Samuel returns with two touchdowns in Dallas
stories.summary: Samuel came back after missing three games with a hamstring injury. He scored the 49ers' first points on an 11-yard catch from Brock Purdy and later broke a 70-yard touchdown run on a reverse. Purdy went 22 of 28 for a career-best 389 yards.

stories.text: 14.5: Points per game the Vikings allow, the NFL's lowest mark
stories.summary: Minnesota owns the league's stingiest scoring defense, run by coordinator Brian Flores. Purdy threw for 319 yards against a Flores defense in 2024 but took a career-high six sacks. The game is at Estadio Banorte, about 7,350 feet above sea level.

stories.text: 49ers face Vikings Sunday night, 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: San Francisco (8-1) plays Minnesota (7-2) at Estadio Banorte in Mexico City on Sunday, Nov. 22. NBC and Peacock carry it. Watch whether the 49ers keep the offense they showed in Dallas against the league's top scoring defense.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Lock keeps Seattle winning while Darnold heals

stories.text: Drew Lock is 4-0 as Seattle's fill-in starter
stories.summary: Lock went 14 of 17 with a 158.0 passer rating in the 21-13 win at Las Vegas. He has seven touchdown passes and no interceptions this season. Mike Macdonald says Sam Darnold is the starter when healthy, so Seattle enters its bye with a settled backup plan.

stories.text: Nelson's return would reshuffle the Seahawks line
stories.summary: Quenton Nelson is recovering from a knee procedure. When he returns he is expected to play left guard, with Grey Zabel moving to right guard. Until then Zabel plays left guard and Anthony Bradford right guard. Josh Jones has started two games at left tackle for Charles Cross, and Bobby Hart filled in for Abraham Lucas.

stories.text: Jaxon Smith-Njigba goes from 11 yards to 171 in one game
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba had one catch for 11 yards at halftime in Las Vegas, then caught seven passes for 160 second-half yards, 144 of them in the third quarter. A 71-yard touchdown highlighted the run. He has 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns through 10 games, a pace of about 2,052 yards. Calvin Johnson's single-season record is 1,964.

stories.text: 6: Sacks of rookie Fernando Mendoza in his first start
stories.summary: Devon Witherspoon had two, both on unblocked cornerback blitzes. Byron Murphy II, Derick Hall, Dante Fowler and DeMarcus Lawrence each added one. Mendoza went 6 of 16 for 53 yards after halftime.

stories.text: Seahawks on bye, then at 49ers Nov. 29 at 4:25 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Seattle (6-4) is off this week, then visits San Francisco (8-1) at Levi's Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29 on FOX. Kickoff is 1:25 p.m. Pacific. Watch Darnold's practice status next week and the line shuffle.
